newsitem.title: CANADA: Agrium outlook for 1997 earnings positive.
newsitem.headline: Agrium outlook for 1997 earnings positive.

text.p: Canadian fertilizer company Agrium Inc, which earlier this month announced a C$1.3-billion merger with Viridian Inc, said on Thursday its outlook for 1997 earnings was positive due to expected high product demand.

"With little improvement in world grain stock ratios despite good world crop yields in 1996, fertilizer application rates will need to continue to increase to maximize agricultural production," Agrium said.

Agrium earlier reported third-quarter earnings of US$0.21 per share, down from US$0.34 per share in the same period last year. Revenues for the period climbed to US$292 million, from US$270 million in 1995.

The company said third-quarter earnings were were lower because of the four-month labor strike in its potash division strike which ended in September, weak ammonia prices in July and a loss of urea production during a one-month shutdown at its Carseland nitrogen plant.
Agrium said it was now focusing its efforts on coastal sites for evaluation of a proposed world-scale nitrogen complex in Argentina.
